nodes.description: External pure function compute(uint256 x) returns uint256 result; evaluates a large polynomial over a prime field using Horner's method implemented in inline assembly.
Input parameter x of compute, the evaluation point of the polynomial; used as the multiplicand in every mulmod Horner iteration.
Local constant PRIME = 0x800000000000011000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000001 used as the modulus for the field arithmetic.
Local accumulator returned by compute; repeatedly updated by the batched Horner iterations and finally reduced modulo PRIME.
Inline assembly block performing chained add/mulmod Horner evaluations over PRIME, operating directly on EVM words without Solidity overflow checks.

edges.reason: Execution of compute flows directly into the inline assembly block that performs the polynomial evaluation.
Caller-supplied argument x is bound to the x parameter of compute before any computation occurs.
Parameter x is consumed inside the assembly as the multiplicand of every mulmod(result, x, PRIME) Horner step.
Local PRIME is consumed inside the assembly as the modulus argument of each mulmod call.
Local result is fed into the assembly as the running accumulator of the Horner iterations.
The assembly block assigns each successive Horner value back to the local result variable.
The value produced by the assembly (result % PRIME) is returned as the output of compute.

normalization_plan.reason: The parameter x is only meaningful as the input of compute and carries no standalone behavior, so it is folded into the function node.
The local constant PRIME is used exclusively as the modulus inside the assembly arithmetic, so it is merged into the unsafe_operation node.
The local accumulator result is mutated and finally produced by the inline assembly, so it is merged into the unsafe_operation node.
